program.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
requirements.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Does chalk-like mark-making render both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene?
nodes.criteria: Pass if chalk-like contours, powdery or broken strokes, layered strokes, or rubbed chalk shading visibly describe both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. These are alternative manifestations of chalk, not features that must all occur everywhere. Broad rubbed shading can qualify when its direction, boundaries, layering or pigment variation describes depicted forms; uniform grain or loss of sharpness alone cannot. Inspect the giraffes separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground: convincing marks in one region cannot substitute for chalk rendering in the other. Fail if either the giraffes or substantial surrounding regions are rendered only by photographic detail, generic grain, blur or smearing without form-describing chalk marks. Color, smooth blended passages, recognizable anatomy and retained composition are permitted. Return unknown only if visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the requested transformation into a drawing made from chalk. Inspect the contours, spots and shading of both giraffes, then inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground for form-describing chalk strokes or rubbed shading rather than merely changed texture.

nodes.question: Are both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene represented through drawn contours, interior marks and shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
nodes.criteria: Pass if drawn contours, interior marks and constructed shading represent both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. Evaluate the giraffes' bodies, spots and legs separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground; neither region alone establishes satisfaction. Broad directional strokes and blended drawn shading may represent simplified environmental forms without preserving fine detail. Fail if substantial areas in either region still depend on retained photographic surface detail or photographic modeling, with only added outlines, grain or blur. Distinguish photographic modeling through retained source-specific detail and tonal structure not re-expressed by drawn marks; accurate anatomy, detailed spots, smooth gradients, dark shading and source resemblance are not by themselves proof of photographic rendering. Texture and smudging alone establish neither drawing nor photography. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient to distinguish the rendering, not simply because different regions provide different evidence.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the requested chalk-drawing transformation. Examine whether the giraffes' contours, body shading and markings are re-expressed as drawn forms, and whether vegetation, hills, sky and ground are independently represented by drawn marks and shading rather than merely softened source detail.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1_drawn_representation: The node’s binding already captures the key regions, but its broad “represented by drawn marks” test appears to over-credit a stylized finish. The traces repeatedly cite outlines, spots, broad strokes, and chalk-like grain, then infer that the whole scene is drawn; they do not separately test whether substantial regions still retain photographic structure. In the edited image, the giraffes and nearby vegetation show clear drawn treatment, while the hills, sky, and ground are largely smeared into broad tonal fields, with source composition and some photographic modeling still apparent. Refine the decision criterion to assess each region independently and distinguish constructed marks/forms from blur, smudging, or texture alone; require evidence that substantial environmental areas have actually been re-expressed, not merely softened. Keep the whole-image completion judgment separate from evidence of partial progress, so strong animal treatment cannot automatically make the entire transformation a pass. The repeated high-confidence “yes” traces despite the partial reference suggest a systematic criterion/binding gap, not a transport or dependency failure; do not treat repetition or confidence as proof of completion.
d1_chalk_medium: The binding already names both giraffes and the surrounding scene, but it needs to prevent strong subject treatment or a generally chalky finish from standing in for completion. Make the decision explicitly region-wise: assess each giraffe and substantial environmental areas separately, and require visible form-describing chalk marks in both, not just softened photographic detail, grain, or broad smearing. In this image, the giraffes and nearby vegetation show clearer drawn treatment, while much of the hills, sky, and ground reads as smeared tonal fields with photographic structure retained; count that as progress, not full fulfillment. Keep the overall completion judgment distinct from evidence of partial progress, and ground it in the actual marks and forms rather than repeated high-confidence votes. Traces are valid observations with no transport, schema, or dependency failures, so address the semantic criterion/binding gap rather than treating this as an execution problem.

findings.source_phrase: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
findings.question: Do the giraffes’ bodies and markings themselves read as chalk-drawn forms, rather than retaining photographic detail beneath outlines or texture?
findings.criteria: Inspect the giraffes separately from the background. Pass if their contours, spots, and body shading are visibly re-expressed through drawn marks; fail if substantial giraffe areas still rely on photographic surface detail or modeling with only outlines, grain, or blur added.
findings.evidence: The edited giraffes retain detailed, sharply patterned spots and dark tonal modeling, while their outlines and some shading appear drawn. This leaves room to distinguish a full chalk rendering of the animals from a photographic-looking base with a drawn treatment over it.
findings.rationale: The existing broad check reports drawn outlines and shading on both giraffes, but does not resolve whether the animals’ interior rendering is itself converted. This is a focused investigation of that evidence, not a presumption that the conversion is incomplete.

transactions.reason: The existing decisions overlap in requiring whole-scene conversion, allowing conspicuous animal outlines and general texture to substitute for independent background evidence. The edited image shows reworked giraffe contours and spot networks, while the hills and ground contain broad streaked tonal fields whose form construction needs separate assessment. Partition the required transformation into subject and environment conditions, including the giraffes' interior rendering rather than assuming outlines establish conversion.

decisions.question: Are both giraffes rendered as chalk-drawn forms, including their contours, markings and body shading?
decisions.criteria: Pass if both giraffes' contours, spot patterns and substantial interior shading are visibly re-expressed as chalk drawing through broken or powdery marks, layered strokes, or form-describing rubbed shading. Inspect each giraffe separately. Outlines alone or a grain overlay on retained photographic interiors do not satisfy this condition. Fail if substantial portions of either giraffe still rely on photographic surface detail or modeling rather than chalk-drawn construction. Detailed spots, dark shading, accurate anatomy and smooth blending are permitted and are not by themselves evidence of retained photography. Return unknown only if the visual evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
decisions.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the instruction 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect both giraffes' contours, necks, torsos, spots and legs, comparing interior rendering as well as edges. Assess the giraffes only; background treatment cannot substitute for their conversion.

decisions.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
decisions.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground separately, including substantial foreground structures. Chalk contours, broken or layered strokes, and rubbed shading may qualify; simplified forms and smooth sky passages are allowed. For broad rubbed passages, look for boundaries, layering or pigment variation that constructs the depicted terrain, vegetation, structures or ground planes, rather than relying solely on source-derived tonal fields. Reduced photographic detail, diagonal streaking, grain or smearing alone does not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas remain photographic modeling softened by blur or texture, even when nearby vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Do not require every area to contain discrete strokes or regard retained composition as evidence of failure. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
decisions.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the instruction 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect the vegetation, distant hills, sky, foreground ground and left-side structure independently of the giraffes. Compare whether environmental forms have been reconstructed in chalk marks or shading, rather than merely losing photographic sharpness.
